Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.
Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Amazon Leo is an ambitious project that depends on entirely new satellite designs along with all of the ground capabilities needed to operate a large constellation and provide high performance service to end users. Because the constellation will have several thousand satellites serving millions of customers, systems are being designed to be highly autonomous, self-adaptable to the environment, and capable of recovery in the event of problems. The great majority of new equipment and software is being developed and built in-house by our engineering and manufacturing teams.
Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) designs the constellation for good coverage and space safety, and develops the systems that control and maneuver each satellite as they ascend from injection to operational orbits, merge into the constellation flow and station keep relative to neighbors. Every spacecraft is ready and able to maneuver at any time to avoid other satellites or space debris if a close pass threatens.
The navigation system provides precise positioning in real-time and supports forecasting future orbital state, taking into account planned maneuvers and other effects. Guidance, Navigation, and Control also provides cueing to direct the communications systems on the satellite that require accurate pointing in order to achieve high performance.
Key job responsibilities
As a Guidance, Navigation, and Control software engineer, you will develop real-time, embedded software that flies the satellite; ground-based applications that predict orbital state, monitor for potential collisions, and optimize maneuvers; high fidelity modeling and simulation software; and all sorts of infrastructure needed to develop and operate the system. Because GNC is the heart of the satellite flight system, you will frequently be pulled in to help with a broad spectrum of problems standing in the way of satellite integration and test, manufacturing, and even flight operations.
A day in the life
This is an opportunity to play a significant role in the design of an entirely new satellite system with challenging performance requirements. The large, integrated constellation brings opportunities for advanced capabilities that need investigation and development. Scale also puts emphasis on engineering excellence so our tools and methods, from conceptualization through manufacturing and all phases of test, will be state of the art as will the satellite and supporting infrastructure on the ground. You will split time working well defined SW projects needed by the program on a schedule, prototyping design concepts that may or may not make it to production, participating in component and satellite level testing, and helping with flight operations.
About the team
Our team has experience with various satellite systems and many other flight vehicles. We have bench strength in our mission, the core Guidance, Navigation, and Control disciplines, and software development for flight and other systems. We design, prototype, test, iterate and learn together. Because GNC is central to safe flight, we tend to drive Concepts of Operation and many system level analyses. You will find that Amazon Leo's mission is compelling, so our program is staffed with some of the top engineers in the industry. Our daily collaboration with other teams on the program brings constant opportunity for discovery, learning, and growth.

- Experience with full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations

AWS operates the world's largest fleet of GPU-accelerated servers for AI/ML training and inference at cloud scale. Our team owns the embedded software that brings these servers up, keeps them healthy, and tells us why they fail. If you want to lead the engineers who write the firmware and diagnostic software underneath frontier model training, this is the role.
We are seeking a Software Development Manager to lead a team of software and systems development engineers working on embedded systems for UltraServer platforms: platform firmware, and other server management software, fleet failure root-causing across hardware, firmware and embedded software failures, and manufacturing test automation. You will set technical direction for your team, deliver embedded software across NPI phases, and own the software side of fleet reliability. The role needs embedded systems depth to guide technical decisions and people leadership to hire, develop and retain a strong engineering team.
What You Will Do
You will lead engineers who own the software layer closest to the hardware. You will set your team's technical strategy for accelerator server platforms with hardware, product and leadership partners, and make trade-offs between schedule, reliability, security and performance. Your team will take the hardest annualized failure rate issues, where the cause could be in silicon, firmware, the kernel or the hypervisor, find the root cause, and turn each finding into diagnostic software that catches the next one automatically. You will also scale manufacturing automation so new platforms ramp with high first-pass yield. You will be accountable for the software contribution to fleet quality.
Why You Will Love It
The world's most advanced frontier models train on servers your team's firmware brings up and keeps healthy. Your diagnostics run across a large fleet of servers, and you can see their effect on failure rates within weeks. The team is technical and high-trust, works closely with hardware and silicon partners, and has direct access to senior leadership.
The Ideal Candidate
You combine embedded systems depth with people leadership. You have led teams that shipped firmware or platform software on server-class hardware, and you can still review a system design, read a kernel log or work through a PCIe link training failure with your engineers. You set a high bar for software quality and security, make decisions with data, and communicate clearly to engineers and executives. You build teams that are stronger because of your presence but don't depend on it.
Key job responsibilities
Technical Leadership & Strategy
1. Set technical direction for software and hardware validation across GPU-accelerated server platforms, including CPU, GPU and NIC interconnects, BMC, BIOS/UEFI integration, CPLD/FPGA interfaces, and power and thermal management firmware
2. Drive architecture and design reviews for platform management software, covering reliability, security, telemetry, and availability.
3. Define software standards for firmware update, recovery and validation that hold across platform generations
4. Reduce duplication so the organization maintains one set of platform software across product lines
Issue Root Cause & Fleet Diagnostics
1. Own a team that root-causes complex fleet failures across hardware, firmware and software layers, including memory errors across CPU and GPU, PCIe link failures and networking interface card failures.
2. Turn root cause findings into durable diagnostic and remediation software that detects recurring failure modes automatically across the fleet.
3. Partner with hardware engineering, silicon vendors and datacenter operations to drive corrective actions into design, firmware and qualification criteria
4. Track annualized failure rate and remediation metrics for software-attributable failures and report trends to leadership
Manufacturing & Test Automation
1. Build and scale manufacturing test and vetting automation with ODM partners to raise first-pass yield and cut test dwell time without losing coverage
2. Deliver firmware flashing, provisioning and configuration workflows used on manufacturing lines and in datacenter bring-up
3. Close the loop between manufacturing escapes, fleet failures and test coverage gaps
People Leadership & Development
1. Hire, develop and retain software and systems development engineers; build a team culture around engineering excellence and customer obsession
2. Set clear goals, give regular feedback, and coach engineers on career growth through 1:1s
3. Run calibrations and promotion assessments and keep the team's technical bar high
4. Build an inclusive environment where engineers can do their best work
Delivery & Cross-Functional Alignment
1. Deliver embedded software across NPI phases (Program Initiation, Design, Qualification, Pilot, Post-GA) in line with hardware schedules
2. Work with hardware engineering, TPMs, EC2, security and datacenter operations teams so platforms are debuggable, serviceable and automation-ready
3. Identify delivery and operational risks early, escalate with data and mitigations, and communicate strategy and status to senior leadership
4. Run operational excellence for owned services, including on-call, post-incident reviews and COEs
May require occasional (<10%) regional and international travel to Design and Manufacturing Partner sites.
A day in the life

Every token a large language model generates depends on data reaching the right accelerator at the right moment. As AI models outgrow any single chip, the network between accelerators becomes the bottleneck that decides how fast — and how affordably — the world's largest models can serve real users. That network layer is what our team builds.
We're in search of an engineer to work at the frontier of disaggregated inference: splitting LLM serving into separate prefill and decode pools and moving the model's KV cache between them at the absolute limit of what the hardware allows. Get it right and users get answers in milliseconds; get it wrong and the fastest accelerators in the world sit idle waiting on data. You'll own pieces of the high-speed transfer path that make the difference, and you'll measure your success in how close you run to the theoretical peak of the machine.
What we're looking for:
Strong C/C++ and a love for low-level, performance-critical systems — solid command of Linux, kernels, memory, and writing fast code. The instinct to ask "how fast could this possibly go?" and the rigor to measure it. Experience with high-speed networking or HPC interconnects (RDMA, InfiniBand, libfabric, UCX, NIXL, MPI) is valued highly; embedded-systems experience is a plus. Prior AI/ML experience is welcome but not required — if you're a great systems engineer, we'll teach you the ML side. If you like solving genuinely hard problems, working shoulder-to-shoulder with HPC and ML customers, iterating fast, and shipping at a scale few places can offer, come join us. This is a role on the leading edge of AI/ML infrastructure.
Key job responsibilities
Build and optimize the low-level data-movement software across accelerators, servers, and heterogeneous memory — over AWS's highest-performance network fabric.
Push performance to the hardware roofline: profile, find the real bottleneck, and close the gap between "it works" and "it runs as fast as physics permits."
Work across the stack — from kernel and network transport up to the inference frameworks — and partner with teams building the chips, runtime, and models.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate these tools. You will turn health signals and network telemetry into operator workflows and automation, proactive health and early warning features, NOC dashboards and runbook automation, alarm correlation and noise reduction, incident management and escalation tooling, and the post-event systems that feed every lesson back into better detection. You will work closely with the product manager, operators, and Call Leaders who use your tools every day, and you will own what you build from design through production.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, and operate scalable, highly available services and tools that power network operations and incident management for Amazon Leo.
- Build proactive health capabilities, including anomaly and trend detection, early warning features, and proactive investigation workflows that help operators act before customers are affected.
- Build alarm correlation and deduplication systems so responders see one problem instead of hundreds of alerts.
- Build NOC dashboards and operator workflows that bring health, customer impact, affected components, and ongoing events into one view.
- Build self-service tooling that lets service teams onboard and manage their own health signals, alarms, and runbooks.
- Automate runbook steps, data collection, and repetitive operational tasks so operators spend their time on judgment, not mechanics.
- Integrate with observability, telemetry, ticketing, paging, and communication systems across Amazon Leo, including the network observability platform.
- Apply automation, machine learning, and generative AI to triage, event summarization, timeline drafting, and correlation where it measurably improves outcomes.
- Design systems that stay available when the network they serve is degraded, since operators need these tools most during an outage.
- Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support.
- Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software.
A day in the life
You might start the day with feedback from the NOC on a dashboard you shipped last week and fix a workflow that slowed operators down during an overnight event. Midday, you could be designing a correlation service that groups alarms from many services into a single event, or building the escalation engine that pages the right leader when an event has been open too long. In the afternoon you might pair with the product manager on a self-service onboarding flow, review code, and prototype an AI-drafted event summary for Call Leaders. Your work shows up every time an issue is caught earlier, resolved faster, or never happens at all.
